items.question: What is ABHA?
items.answer: ABHA stands for Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA).

items.question: What if I forget my ABHA Number or I misplace my card?
items.answer: There is no need to worry. You can retrieve your 14-digit ABHA Number from your ABHA address. You can recover your account either using your Aadhaar number or registered mobile Number. Recovery using any of the above methods requires filling out your basic details and access to your linked mobile.

items.question: What should I do if I forget my password?
items.answer: You can login to your ABHA Number through Mobile OTP or Aadhaar linked Mobile OTP, as applicable, and set a new password.

items.question: What information/documents are required for creating an ABHA Number?
items.answer:
ABHA number can be generated in two ways i.e. via Aadhaar and Driving licence in self-registration mode:
Documents required while creating ABHA number through Aadhaar Card:

Aadhaar Number
Mobile number linked with Aadhaar number
Documents required while creating ABHA number through Driving License:
Driving license
Name
DOB
Gender
Going forward additional options to authenticate your identity shall also be provided.

items.question: There is only one mobile device in my family. How do I create an ABHA and authenticate the same for my other family members?
items.answer: One mobile number can generate ABHA number of 6 members.

items.question: I am afraid that by linking all my health records to my ABHA other doctors may be in a position to see all my medical history which I don’t want to show. How can this be prevented?
items.answer: The consent provided digitally need not be for all the health records linked to ABHA at a time. It can be provided for sharing only selected health records as per the choice of the patient. Therefore, by linking all your health records to your ABHA you will not end up sharing all your health records when providing consent. The consent is granular  “which can be provided separately for each of the health record as per the wish of the patient”. However, it is recommended that you provide consent to share all health records with your doctor so that he can make correct clinical decision.

items.question: If I have all my records linked with only one ABHA address , will that compromise my data which I don’t want to share with my healthcare providers?
items.answer:
ABDM provides the option to an individual to share only those records with healthcare providers which he/she wishes to. However, in such case, the healthcare provider (doctor) may not be able to make the best clinical judgment and the responsibility of such clinical decision will be on the patient (for failure to disclose the complete medical history). Therefore, even though such a feature is available, patients are advised to share all the records with their doctors.
It is also possible for you to link all your health records with one ABHA address and at the same time share only some of these health records with your healthcare provider. This is possible because the consent is “granular”, which means that consent for each record can be given separately.

items.question: How do I create my ABHA Address?
items.answer:
An ABHA Address can be created through a PHR Application (such as ABHA Mobile Application). Further, there are two ways to create an ABHA Address:
a.) By using your allotted ABHA Number.
b.)	By self-declaring your information like your Name, Email-id/ Mobile Number, Gender, etc. through a PHR application (like ABHA Mobile App).

items.question: What is ABHA Number?
items.answer: An individual/citizen/patient is provided with a randomly generated fourteen-digit number which is known as ABHA. This number is used for the purpose of uniquely identifying a person in the digital health ecosystem, authenticate him/her and link his/her health records with consent across multiple systems and stakeholders. This helps create their longitudinal health records across different healthcare providers which facilitates better delivery of healthcare to them.

items.question: Is it mandatory for all citizens to get an ABHA Number?
items.answer: No, it is not mandatory for all citizens to get an ABHA Number. Whoever wishes to participate in the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and wishes to have their records available digitally may create an ABHA. .

items.question: Is my ABHA Number unique?
items.answer: Yes, the ABHA Number of an individual is a 14-digit randomly generated unique number.

items.question: What is HIE-CM?
items.answer:
Health Information Exchange and Consent Manager (HIE-CM) is a digital system developed by ABDM. It enables consent management, linking, and sharing of personal health records for users.
Currently there is one HIE-CM which has been developed by the government. All the PHR addresses generated using this HIE-CM are of the format abc@abdm. Multiple consent managers provided by different agencies may also come up in the coming few months. The user shall be free to choose whichever HIE-CM they want to use.

items.question: My Mobile Number is not linked to my Aadhaar Number. How do I authenticate my Aadhaar for ABHA Number creation?
items.answer:
It is recommended that your mobile number is linked with Aadhaar. You can do so by visiting nearest Permanent Aadhaar Centre.
Alternatively, if your Aadhaar is not linked to any mobile number, you can also visit the nearest participating facility and opt for biometric authentication using Aadhaar Number. After successful authentication, you will obtain an ABHA Number at the facility itself.

items.question: Why should I create an ABHA Number?
items.answer: Creating an ABHA Number is your starting point in the journey of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. By generating an ABHA number, you get the option to create an ABHA address which allows you to store all your digital health records at one place and share these records with hospitals/doctors you visit, with your consent, with suitable applications. Going forward, it will also help you in booking your hospital appointments online and avail healthcare services digitally.

items.question: How is consent taken while using Aadhaar for creation of ABHA?
items.answer: Every Aadhaar number can be linked with a mobile number. The consent is sought by submitting the OTP (one-time password) received on your Aadhaar linked mobile number while creating your ABHA. Digital health solution providers are also being encouraged to provide other features of providing consent through the use of biometric authentications using fingerprint, facial authentication etc.

items.question: What health data will be stored in the ABDM ecosystem?
items.answer:
Any health data that is made available digitally can be stored on a suitable application compatible with the ABDM ecosystem. Types of health records can include your prescriptions, discharge summary, lab reports, vaccination summary, CT scans, MRI scans etc. Click here to read about federated architecture of ABDM for storage of data.
( https://sandbox.abdm.gov.in/docs/architecture)

items.question: Are my health records safe and secure?
items.answer:
ABDM does not store any health records. Health records are always created and stored by healthcare providers within their internal ecosystem as per their retention policies. ABDM only facilitates secure data exchange between the intended stakeholders on ABDM network after the patient’s consent. Hence, through ABDM compliant applications, patients will also be able to choose which the health records which they want linked with their ABHA, securely store their digital health records on their devices, securely access their records online, and securely share their health records with healthcare providers after giving consent. Click here to read about federated architecture of ABDM for storage of data.
( https://sandbox.abdm.gov.in/docs/architecture)

items.question: Why has the government come out with an ABHA Number when almost all residents in India have an Aadhaar number which is already unique?
items.answer:
The purpose of creating Aadhar is restrictive in purpose of namely, establishing identity of an individual as a condition for receipt of a subsidy, benefit or service for which the expenditure is incurred from, or the receipt there from forms part of etc. Using Aadhaar number is voluntary by individuals to establish their identities.
Hence, an alternative other than Aadhaar (i.e. ABHA Number) has been created. Aadhaar can be linked with such ABHA Number and ABDM recommends that your ABHA Number should be linked with Aadhaar. This will enable you to login into the system using Aadhaar number in case you forget your ABHA Number or ABHA address.

items.question: Is ABHA Number and Ayushman card/Golden card issued by National Health Authority (NHA) same or different.?
items.answer:
These two are different.
The National Health Authority implements two distinct health programs:
a. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)– This is a program aimed at providing health cover of Rs 5 Lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. Under this program, the beneficiaries are entitled for getting an Ayushman card (earlier known as Golden Card).
b. National Health Authority is entrusted with  implementing Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (earlier known as National Digital Health Mission). ABDM was rolled out throughout India on 27th September 2021. Under ABDM, all citizens can create ABHA Number.

items.question: I am facing a problem creating or accessing my ABHA Number? What should I do?
items.answer: You can either speak at our call center number, 1800-11-4477 / 14477 or can file an online grievance at https://grievance.abdm.gov.in/

items.question: Do I have to submit any physical documents?
items.answer: No, you are not required to submit any physical documents anywhere. Creation of ABHA Number is fast, paperless and hassle free.

items.question: Will I be denied treatment/healthcare services if I do not have an ABHA Number?
items.answer: No.

items.question: How much time will it take for registration to complete?
items.answer: Complete registration for ABHA Number can be done within 5 minutes as you are only required to fill your basic details and authenticate your KYC document.

items.question: Is it necessary for me to remember my fourteen-digit ABHA Number for using services through ABDM?
items.answer: No. A fourteen-digit ABHA Number is generated only to provide a unique identity to an individual. You can use your fourteen-digit number while using the systems.

items.question: Do I need to print/ carry a physical copy of my ABHA Number card?
items.answer:
There is no need for printing of your ABHA Number card. You may keep the copy of ABHA Number digital card in your phone. You can also write the number at a convenient place. However, if you wish so, you can take print out of the digital card and keep it for your convenience.
Users can also choose to create an ABHA Address (Personal Health Record address)  such as “ajay@abdm”. Hence, users are not required to remember their ABHA, and can use their ABHA address.

items.question: What is an ABHA Address?
items.answer: ABHA Address can be created for the purpose of an individual’s Personal Health Records (PHR). It is a unique address similar to a virtual payment address or email ID which is created by an individual, as per their choice. This is provided to facilitate linking, sharing and storing of an individual PHR in a secure manner. It can also be linked to one’s ABHA Number.  Also, it is easier to remember such an address rather than remembering a fourteen-digit ABHA Number. For example - ajay@abdm, abc@abdm, etc.

items.question: How are ABHA Number and ABHA address linked?
items.answer: Post creation of ABHA Address, you can link your ABHA Address, or several ABHA Addresses created by you with your respective ABHA Number allotted to you,  through the ABHA Mobile Application (PHR Application) or via visiting  phr.abdm.gov.in.

items.question: Will I get free treatment/healthcare services if I have an ABHA Number?
items.answer: No. ABHA Number only provides a unique identity of the person in digital health ecosystem. Cost of the treatment, free or otherwise, is decided by policies of respective healthcare providers and schemes.

items.question: How many ABHA addresses can be linked to one ABHA Number?
items.answer: There is no limitation for linkage of ABHA addresses with ABHA number.

items.question: Is it necessary to have an ABHA Number in order to create an ABHA address/addresses?
items.answer: No , ABHA address can separately be created via going to https://phr.abdm.gov.in

items.question: I no longer want to participate in ABDM. Can I opt out my ABHA Number?
items.answer: ABDM supports a feature that enables any participating user to opt out of the ABDM ecosystem. On availing the feature, a user can deactivate/ opt out their ABHA Number.
